text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein meets British Prime Minister John Major and puts emphasis in talks in London "on need to intensify efforts towards achieving comprehensive and just peace in Middle East".
- In view of a drop in world grain prices and the purchase of 150,000 tonnes of wheat, a reduction in bread prices is possible soon.
- Crown Prince Hassan departs to a number of European states on a private visit accompanied by his wife Princess Tharwat.
- Queen Noor, during a charity dinner in Toronto to support Middle East students scholarships in Canada, stresses the importance of education in the promotion of the forces of peace.
- Jordan renews its demands to implement the Oslo accord and close the Jerusalem tunnel, and Prime Minister Kabariti says "the situation in Palestinian territories is open to all the possibilities".
- Opposition says Jordanian criticism of Israel is not sufficient and "what is required is translating it into action".

- Al-Rai talks to political figures who say King Hussein's policy is characterised by moderation and decisiveness and that Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's policies are closing the door towards peace paths.
- Cold front is on its way to Jordan.
- Jordanian-Palestinian meeting next Monday, and PLO officials say Hussein and Arafat to discuss a unified stance towards Israeli intransigence. Israeli president to visit Amman this week.
- King Hussein delivers pressure on Netanyahu within Israel and inside Jewish American and British lobby.
- Ministry of Trade says capitalisation tax imposed on companies will be abolished in new companies law.
